expectedBehavior: P1 freezes every command and every UI-required task read before implementation, including six independent inventory detail reads and a complete copy preflight.
Every one of the 42 operations has one explicit face, accountable owner or coordinator boundary, authorization source, request/response shape, typed failures and primary scenario bindings.
The copy preflight compares every reused object whose same matching tuple can change business meaning, rewrites every outbound reference, and rejects stale source or target facts before any write.
C-16, C-17 and C-19 remain identical across IA, contract, database invariants, UI behavior and API/L2 evidence.
P1, P2 and P3 consume one immutable canonical fixture/scenario catalog while seedDatasets and negative testDatasets remain disjoint.
Each stage has one owner for every mutable source, an exact evidence denominator, and an honest business/cleanup boundary.
blindReviewDeclaration: The reviewer read the requirement, IA, Dexter rulings, repository standards and current source structure first, independently derived the expected architecture, counterexamples and smaller alternative, and only then read design 22086ea88e489efb025cdb6e5c7dab61f15ccaac73d3063d3dd4fe441dad54bc and manifest 56510928ba97f94b977e47296309bf10c5f0863b1d8d4943ef32160a7af80923. No author intake, handoff or author verdict was read.

falsificationResults.evidence: Design sections 3.3-3.4 enumerate write operations, workbench/detail reads, six inventory sections and copy preflight fields, but C-17 void/recreate is not given an executable command/state contract.

Section 3.3 expands 42 unique operationIds and all are operations-admin-only; asset staging/release is justified by the approved multi-image lifecycle and remains asset-owned. However there is no per-operation owner/coordinator, authorization/capability, request/response, error and scenario row, so ownership correctness cannot be recomputed.
The stage-by-IU prose is directionally sound, but the mutable CRUD policy is assigned to P1 and again to P3, and the manifest P2 ordered chain still says 26/89 while the frozen denominator is 26/91.

One schema-bound catalog separates legal seedDatasets from negative testDatasets, requires consumer SHA/revision readback, and generates stale/limit failures through owner actions rather than contaminating DEV seed.

The frozen vectors arithmetically recompute to 26 definitions/91 API cases and 18 definitions/43 L2 cases, and the API/L2 responsibility split is reasonable. The manifest retains one stale 26/89 execution string, so the denominator is not exact across all owning bytes.

Category, catalog tag and SKU sales attribute correctly have no approved structural bits, but ProductSku is copied and reused by (itemCode, skuCode) while its attributeValueRefs can differ; that semantic collision is absent from compatibility classification.

C-16 visible-disabled and C-19 no StockTarget code are traced across contract/UI/API/DB. C-17 forbids code in update shapes but does not freeze the zero-reference void/recreate command, state transition, reference judgment and evidence denominator.

Closure, full reference rewriting, digest/version vector, REQUIRED atomic execution, idempotency and source/target TOCTOU are correctly assigned to P2 while P3 only proves interaction. SKU semantic compatibility remains an uncovered blocker inside that P2 closure.
Three fact owners, a stateless assetless app coordinator, owner public APIs, task reads, one REQUIRED transaction, one Flyway history and no cross-schema DML/MQ form a coherent acyclic topology.

The definition-only P1, API-business P2 and local-browser L2 P3 boundaries are honest and business/cleanup are separated. Duplicate policy ownership and the stale P2 denominator prevent exact package exits.

findings.title: The 42-operation denominator is named but not ownership- and authorization-deterministic
findings.evidence: Design section 3.3 lists 42 operationIds and section 1.3 globally says operations-admin face plus catalog/inventory/fulfillment-production owners. It does not bind each operation to x-owner-module or coordinator status, authorization/capability source, request/response component, typed error exact-set and primary scenario. The ambiguous rows include getOperationsCatalogWorkbenchContext (organization/workspace facts), saveOperationsCatalogItem (catalog+inventory coordinator), executeOperationsBrandCatalogCopy (three-owner coordinator), two asset operations, diagnostics and shape manifest.
findings.risk: P1 can reach count 42 while assigning an operation to the wrong owner, duplicating authorization truth at the coordinator, or omitting a required typed failure; generated consumers and P2 controllers would then faithfully implement incompatible ownership.
findings.counterexample: A contract can mark executeOperationsBrandCatalogCopy as catalog-owned and let the catalog adapter interpret production-tag and inventory authorization while still satisfying the global three-owner prose, operation count and operations-admin face count.
findings.reason: An implementation-facing contract denominator must make per-operation ownership and security mechanically recomputable, not merely inferable from naming groups.
findings.minimalRepair: Add one checked 42-row operation matrix keyed by operationId with face, owner or explicit APP_COORDINATOR, participating owners, capability/page source, request/response components, exact typed failures and primary API/L2 scenario IDs; generate the grouped prose/count from that matrix.
findings.largerAlternativeCost: Separate catalogs per owner or per page would duplicate shared operations and make cross-owner commands harder to audit; one flat checked matrix is smaller.

findings.title: Copy compatibility omits a semantic ProductSku collision
findings.evidence: Requirements section 5.6.3 puts SKU in the closure and requires rewriting its owner item ref and attribute value refs; ProductSku also has an enabled attribute-value combination uniqueness rule. C-19 matches an existing SKU by (itemCode, skuCode). The nine-class matrix and design sections 3.6-3.7 classify SKU attribute values but contain no ProductSku compatibility result.
findings.risk: A target SKU with the same itemCode+skuCode but different attributeValueRefs can be silently reused. The copied BOM or composite reference then points at a target specification different from the source specification the user confirmed.
findings.disposition: OPEN; requires source-based author intake and Dexter decision because adding ProductSku changes the approved nine-class compatibility denominator.
findings.counterexample: Source LATTE/LARGE means size=LARGE, while the store already has LATTE/LARGE bound to size=MEDIUM. Matching succeeds by C-19, all existing nine compatibility checks can pass, and references rewrite to a semantically different SKU.
findings.reason: The three NOT_APPLICABLE_NO_STRUCTURAL_BITS classifications for category, catalog tag and SKU sales attribute are valid; the missing blocker is a tenth copied object type, not a reason to invent structural bits for those three.
findings.minimalRepair: Either add ProductSku compatibility with its parent item identity plus canonical attribute-value combination as structural bits, or prove and enforce an invariant that makes the counterexample impossible before preflight; update scenario and denominator counts from the chosen ruling.
findings.largerAlternativeCost: Treating every SKU field as structural would overblock harmless display differences; a narrow canonical combination check is cheaper.

findings.title: C-17 zero-reference void-and-recreate has no executable lifecycle contract
findings.evidence: Design sections 3.5 and 7 correctly remove code from update requests and state that an erroneous code is corrected only by voiding a zero-reference record and recreating it. The 42 operations only expose generic item/category/dictionary/production-tag status transitions and nested saveOperationsCatalogItem; no void state/command, zero-reference judgment, failure code, per-type applicability, replacement readback or focused scenario is defined.
findings.risk: Implementers can choose archive, deactivate, physical delete, unrestricted replacement or no correction path at all, while still passing the closed update-schema check. C-17 would be consistent only in prose, not across contract/DB/UI/test.
findings.counterexample: A mistyped SalesUnit code has zero references. The update DTO correctly lacks code, but transitionOperationsCatalogDictionaryEntryStatus only supports ACTIVE/INACTIVE; the user cannot perform the approved void-and-recreate recovery without an unplanned API or physical deletion.
findings.reason: Immutable code and a usable correction path are one product ruling; freezing only the prohibition leaves the required recovery behavior undefined.
findings.minimalRepair: Freeze the exact VOID/ARCHIVE semantic, applicable object types including nested SKU/value records, owner reference-count judgment, typed referenced/conflict failures, replacement creation/readback and API/L2 cases; reuse existing transition/save operations only if their closed request/state shapes explicitly cover it.
findings.largerAlternativeCost: Adding dedicated void endpoints for every type is unnecessary if one typed transition family and nested aggregate command can express the same invariant.

findings.title: The P2 manifest still executes the superseded 26/89 denominator
findings.evidence: Frozen design sections 3.7, 3.9, 4.5, 4.6, 6, 8 and 9 consistently use 26 definitions/91 API cases, and the manifest approvedAssertions/evidence also use 91. Manifest deliveryUnits[CATALOG-INVENTORY-BACKEND-U02].orderedChain still says run 26 and 89 API denominator.
findings.risk: The package-exit source can accept 89 cases or produce contradictory automation depending on whether the runner consumes approvedAssertions or orderedChain.
findings.counterexample: A P2 runner executes 89 cases and points to the manifest ordered chain while the evidence block expects 91; both claims are present in the same frozen manifest.
findings.reason: A denominator exact-set cannot contain two totals in its owning manifest.
findings.minimalRepair: Change the ordered chain to 26/91 and add one manifest self-check that every occurrence of the API definition/case denominator equals the canonical scenario vector sum.
findings.largerAlternativeCost: A new scenario registry is unnecessary for this defect; one canonical numeric field plus generated prose is sufficient.

findings.title: CRUD policy mutation is owned by both P1 and P3
findings.evidence: Design sections 2.1, 3.9, 8 and manifest U01 changeSurfaces assign contracts/policy/crud-presentation-standard-catalog.json to P1 before contract/fixture work. Design section 5.1 again requires P3's first actual change to update the same policy, and manifest U03 orderedChain says register policy and pages even though U03 does not list the policy change surface.
findings.risk: P3 either mutates a P1-frozen source without reopening P1 or has no authorized change surface for its first ordered action; IU-stage exact-set and canonical SHA consumption cease to be truthful.
findings.counterexample: P1 closes with the product-workbench surface registered. P3 edits the same policy again to register implementation paths, causing P2/P3 to consume a different policy hash while still claiming P1 bytes are unchanged.
findings.reason: A shared mutable source must have one stage owner; later stages may verify or consume it but cannot silently repeat its mutation.
findings.minimalRepair: Choose one owner. Recommended: P1 freezes the policy surface classification and all target source identifiers; P3 only verifies those entries against actual paths. If an implementation-path field cannot exist before P3, model it as a separately owned generated binding that does not rewrite the P1 policy truth.
findings.largerAlternativeCost: Merging P1 and P3 would remove the duplicate handoff but destroy the useful contract-before-UI boundary; single ownership plus read-only verification is smaller.

solutionReasonableness.problemFit: The three-stage split fits the real task: contract and fixtures first, owner/API closure second, browser interaction last. It correctly keeps copy algorithms out of the browser and preserves owner boundaries.
solutionReasonableness.simplerAlternativeAssessment: A smaller representation is one checked assertion matrix keyed by assertionId with IA ID, IU, stage, operation, owner, source, fixture and primary scenario columns; grouped IU/stage prose should be generated views. This is simpler and less drift-prone than maintaining parallel P1/P2/P3, IU and manifest strings. Collapsing to two delivery stages was considered and rejected because combining contract definition with backend implementation would remove the useful fail-closed boundary that prevents DTO and fixture invention.
solutionReasonableness.costFit: The architecture is proportionate, but the five bounded repairs are cheaper than allowing copy corruption, an unusable immutable-code recovery path, and denominator drift into implementation.

conclusion.summary: DESIGN Round 1 is NO_GO: M=3, S=2, N=0. The three-stage architecture is sound, but per-operation ownership, ProductSku compatibility and C-17 recovery are not implementation-deterministic; two manifest/stage exact-set drifts also remain.
conclusion.authorizationBoundary: Design review only. This verdict authorizes no implementation, contract or policy mutation, generated output, schema or migration, seed or reset, DEV/UAT/L2, environment action, deployment, or repository-control action.
